demonstration_summary.title: Alert triage complete
demonstration_summary.summary: The walkthrough triaged “${scenario.title}” without treating a fired rule as sufficient proof of a current incident. It opened the run-scoped alert, separated status from the reason it fired, and followed the alert to source evidence before classifying it as ${truth.finding} with ${truth.scope}.

checks.title: Alert identity and status
checks.detail: The controller-provisioned alert for this run was opened and its current status and execution time were checked. That removed unrelated rule history and established whether the condition was still active, while deliberately leaving customer impact unproven.

checks.title: Rule reason
checks.detail: The alert’s Reason and recent execution were interpreted together to identify the value, threshold, or event that produced the signal. This distinguished an active scenario condition from an earlier firing, a recovered state, or a superficially similar alert title.

checks.title: Source evidence
checks.detail: The alert’s source link was followed with its query and time context preserved. A matching event, trace, or metric independently corroborated ${truth.scope}, testing whether ${truth.finding} represents real impact rather than only a derived alert document.

demonstration_summary.evidence: The alert identity and execution state establish the correct rule context, its reason explains the triggering condition, and the matching source record independently establishes impact. Those layers agree on ${truth.finding} and ${truth.scope}, so the decision is supported beyond the alert title or status alone.
demonstration_summary.conclusion: ${truth.conclusion} The alert explains why the condition was detected, and the matching source evidence justifies the final classification and priority.

answer.evidence: The alert and matching source event justify classifying it as ${truth.finding} with ${truth.scope}.

goals.title: Open the run alert
goals.concept: Alert status is meaningful only with its rule reason and execution time.
goals.narration: Find and open the controller-provisioned alert.
goals.reasoning: The run-scoped rule avoids unrelated alert history.
goals.evidence: The alert detail belongs to this run.

demonstration.narration: Find and open the controller-provisioned alert for “${scenario.title}”. We will start with the alert created for this run before deciding whether it is ${truth.finding}.
demonstration.reasoning: The Alerts table can contain executions from different rules and times. Opening the run-scoped row prevents unrelated alert history from influencing our decision about ${truth.scope}.
demonstration.evidence: The detail view should identify this run’s alert and show its current state and execution time. That confirms we have the correct alert, but status alone does not yet prove customer impact.

goals.title: Interpret status and reason
goals.concept: Status says whether the condition is active; reason explains what crossed the condition.
goals.narration: Inspect the alert reason and execution history.
goals.reasoning: A fired rule is not automatically a current customer incident.
goals.evidence: The reason and timing establish the alert condition.

demonstration.narration: Inspect the alert’s Reason and most recent execution. The status tells us whether the condition is active; the reason tells us what value or event crossed the rule’s condition.
demonstration.reasoning: A rule may have fired earlier, recovered, or matched harmless data. Separating current status from the reason is necessary before treating ${truth.finding} and ${truth.scope} as a defensible triage classification.
demonstration.evidence: The reason and execution time should establish the scenario signal behind the alert. We now know why it fired, but we still need a source event outside the alert document to corroborate impact.

hints: Separate the rule state from its interpretation.

goals.title: Pivot to source evidence
goals.concept: Triage requires a source event, trace, or metric beyond the alert itself.
goals.narration: Follow the alert to matching source evidence.
goals.reasoning: The pivot verifies whether the condition represents customer impact.
goals.evidence: The source result corroborates the triage decision.

demonstration.narration: Follow the alert’s source link while preserving its query and time context. We expect a real event, trace, or metric that independently supports ${truth.scope}.
demonstration.reasoning: An alert is a derived signal, not the underlying incident evidence. Checking the source prevents us from classifying it from its title alone and tests whether ${truth.finding} reflects current customer impact.
demonstration.evidence: The matching source result should corroborate the condition described by the alert. Alert context plus source evidence supports the triage decision: ${truth.conclusion}

goals.reasoning: A justified priority connects alert context to customer impact.
goals.evidence: The response cites alert and source evidence.
